items.title: Singapore construction waste resurfaces at closed Pontian dumping site
items.summary: PONTIAN: Suspected construction waste from Singapore has resurfaced at a previously closed dumping site in Rimba Terjun here, with 10 lorries linked to various companies detected during an enforcement operation. Johor Solid Waste Management and Public Cleansing Corporation (SWCorp) director Zainal Fitri Ahmad said 8 of the lorries had records showing they entered Malaysia carrying stone waste, involving four companies. Zainal, who led the enforcement operation at Lot 3700, Mukim Rimba Terjun, on Nov 13, said it followed public complaints about suspected illegal waste dumping.

items.title: Flash floods, fallen trees disrupt traffic in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A heavy late-afternoon downpour caused flash floods along several major roads and uprooted trees at multiple locations in Tanjung Bungah and Paya Terubong today. State Infrastructure Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said emergency response teams were deployed to clear fallen trees and manage traffic flow. He said a traffic light malfunction was also reported at the junction leading to the Tanjung Bungah market, further slowing evening rush-hour traffic.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 18, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Ismail told to continue as MB Tuanku Muhriz has reportedly instructed Ismail Lasim to continue as Negri Sembilan menteri besar, with his position still unresolved. Anwar calls for fairer trade At the Apec CEO Summit, Anwar Ibrahim urged global leaders to promote fairer trade and share technology with developing economies. Penang street makes global top 10 Penang's Beach Street has been ranked ninth on Time Out's list of the world's 28 coolest streets for 2026.

items.title: Rare earths: Radzi warns against repeating colonial-era tin history
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must not repeat its colonial-era experience with tin mining in developing its rare earth industry, Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Md Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) has warned. He questioned the extent of the Science, Technology and Innovation Ministry's (Mosti) involvement in research and development (R&D) into rare earth processing. Radzi said growing interest from world powers in Malaysia's rare earth deposits was evident, noting that 80 per cent of the deposits were located in Terengganu, Kelantan, Perak, Kedah and Pahang, within forest reserves.

items.title: Lac Med secures RM21.2mil contract for angiography systems at three hospitals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lac Med Bhd has secured a RM21.2 million contract to supply and integrate advanced angiography systems for cardiology and interventional radiology across three public hospitals in Malaysia. The contract was awarded to its subsidiary, Lac Medical Supplies Sdn Bhd, by a local healthcare project partner. The latest contract follows another healthcare technology contract announced on Monday, bringing the group's order book to a record high of more than RM300 million.

items.title: Prosper Trading secures 56.45pct stake in United Malacca, takeover offer unconditional
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prosper Trading Sdn Bhd, together with its co-founders Tee Kim Tee @ Tee Ching Tee and Tee Cheng Hua, has acquired a collective 118.41 million shares, representing a 56.45 per cent stake in United Malacca Bhd, making its takeover offer for the plantation company unconditional. In a statement, UOB Kay Hian (M) Sdn Bhd, on behalf of the offerors, said the acceptance condition was met today after the offerers' aggregate shareholding in United Malacca exceeded the required 50 per cent threshold. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Guan Chong's Q3 net profit surges more than sixfold to RM277.65mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Guan Chong Bhd's net profit surged more than sixfold to RM277.65 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM41.24 million a year earlier, driven by effective management of raw material purchases and cocoa ingredient sales positions. Revenue, meanwhile, fell 38 per cent to RM2.31 billion from RM3.73 billion a year earlier, due to lower selling prices for cocoa products in line with declining cocoa bean prices. For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, Guan Chong's net profit rose to RM654.25 million from RM184.04 million a year earlier, while revenue declined to RM6.73 billion from RM11.92 billion.

items.title: Form Three student found dead at Kuala Kangsar boarding school
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR: A Form Three student at a fully residential school here was found dead on the school grounds today. Several police vehicles were seen entering the school compound this evening, believed to be in connection with investigations into the incident. However, police have yet to issue an official statement or provide details surrounding the incident.

items.title: Policeman killed in motorcycle collision with car in Kota Baru
items.summary: Corporal Muhamad Alimi Kamarudin, 35, died at the scene in the 5.15pm collision after sustaining serious head and body injuries. He was attached to the weapons division at the Kota Baru district police station. Kota Baru district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Azmir Damiri confirmed the incident, saying police would issue a statement soon.

items.title: Hong Leong Industries posts higher net profit of RM163.67mil in Q1
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Industries Bhd posted a higher net profit of RM163.67 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q1 2027) compared with RM154.90 million in the same period last year. Revenue rose to RM997.18 million in 1Q 2027 from RM983.38 million previously, primarily attributed to a better sales mix of motorcycle models and lower raw material costs resulting from favourable foreign exchange movements. Hong Leong Industries declared an interim single-tier dividend of 35 sen per share for the quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, to be paid on Dec 16, 2026.

items.title: Man killed after tree crushes motorcycle in Selayang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A man died when a tree fell and crushed the motorcycle he was riding at Jalan Set 2/8, Setia Eco Templer, Selayang, this afternoon. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 2.19pm. He said six personnel and two fire engines from the Selayang Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene.

items.title: LTAT: Size not sole criterion in Boustead Plantations takeover bids
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The bidding process for the takeover of Boustead Plantations Bhd is not based solely on the size of the bidder but also takes into account other criteria, the Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) said. LTAT, which controls Boustead Plantations, said its key investment activities were carried out through a competitive bidding process guided by pre-established evaluation criteria, with an emphasis on integrity and good governance. The fund said bidders must be either government-linked companies (GLCs) or Bumiputera-owned companies, or both, with their status verified by an independent third-party adviser.

items.title: JS Solar secures RM30mil rooftop solar, battery storage contract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: JS Solar Holding Bhd's unit JS Solar Sdn Bhd has secured a RM30 million contract from NUR Power Ventures Sdn Bhd for a rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (Bess) project. JS Solar Holding said the contract marked further progress in its collaboration with NUR Power Sdn Bhd, the holding company of NUR Power Ventures. JS Solar Holding managing director Johnson Chai Jeun Sian said the latest contract would strengthen the company's capabilities in integrated renewable energy solutions.

items.title: 4 policemen injured in Tapah van crash discharged from hospital
items.summary: IPOH: Four of the 10 policemen injured in an accident involving a police van at Km352 of the North-South Expressway (southbound), near Tapah, yesterday, have been discharged from Tapah Hospital today. He said four of them were being treated at Slim River Hospital, while the other two were undergoing treatment at Tapah Hospital and Teluk Intan Hospital. The 10 other policemen in the van sustained injuries, with four suffering serious injuries and six sustaining minor injuries.

items.title: UK cyber safety agency urges firms to limit vulnerabilities after Java warning
items.summary: LONDON: Britain's National Cyber Security Centre on Wednesday urged organisations to keep systems updated and reduce exposure to cyberattacks after US and South Korean authorities warned of critical vulnerabilities in the widely used Java programming language. "We would urge organisations to continue to follow vendor best practice advice and keep their systems up-to-date, as part of the ongoing patch wave," NCSC Chief Technology Officer Ollie Whitehouse said. — REUTERS © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: MACC ends cooperation with Bachar Kiwan after obtaining Kuwait records
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has ended its cooperation with businessman Bachar Kiwan after obtaining official documents and verified records from Kuwaiti authorities for investigations into the recovery of assets linked to 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB). The commission said the documents were obtained through a Mutual Legal Assistance (MLA) request to Kuwait, making information provided by Kiwan no longer essential to its investigations. In a statement today, MACC said it had also conducted an internal investigation into several allegations made by Kiwan, as reported by Sarawak Report since Aug 16.

items.title: Citaglobal unit to acquire remaining 45pct stake in Germany's Lawi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Citaglobal Bhd's unit Citaglobal Environment Management Sdn Bhd is acquiring the remaining 45 per cent stake in German waste-to-energy (WTE) technology firm Lawi Engineering GmbH for about RM4.32 million. Separately, Citaglobal Environment will subscribe for 150,000 new Lawi shares at €1 each, totalling €150,000 (RM681,855). Upon completion, Lawi will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Citaglobal Environment.

items.title: Anwar highlights Malaysia's resilient Q3 growth, 'centrality' policy to woo investors in Shenzhen
items.summary: SHENZHEN: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim addressed business leaders from Malaysia and China emphasising Malaysia's robust economic trajectory and a pragmatic foreign policy as key pillars for foreign investment. The prime minister underscored the Malaysia's positive economic momentum by crediting it to stable governance and thriving international partnerships. Anwar tied this economic resilience to Malaysia's proactive international engagement, with China playing an important role in both trade and investments.

items.title: State secretary unaware of Ismail's resignation as MB
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim said neither he nor his office had received any information about a resignation letter submitted by Datuk Ismail Lasim as menteri besar. "I have not received any information about Ismail intending to resign as Negri Sembilan menteri besar. The event was officiated by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

items.title: MGB's Q3 net profit inches up amid weaker construction revenue
items.summary: Revenue fell 30.6 per cent to RM157.7 million from RM227.2 million, mainly due to lower contributions from local construction and property development activities. Revenue declined to RM569.5 million from RM671.3 million in the same period. Meanwhile, property development revenue declined to RM200.38 million from RM300.98 million, while pre-tax profit fell to RM23.75 million from RM40.81 million.

items.title: No major cyber threats affecting Malaysians detected so far, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: No significant cyber threats affecting the people's data or the country's digital infrastructure have been detected so far, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said claims of Malaysians' data being leaked on several dark web sites had yet to be verified, while the National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) had not reported any such incidents. Commenting on the government's proactive measures to monitor and address global cyber threats, Fahmi said that Malaysia was accelerating its transition to quantum-safe telecommunications systems and infrastructure.

items.title: Pecca's Q1 net profit falls 28.4pct on weaker automotive orders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pecca Group Bhd's net profit dropped 28.4 per cent to RM11.01 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM15.39 million a year earlier, on lower revenue. Revenue fell 14 per cent to RM52.14 million from RM60.6 million in the same period due to softer order volumes in the group's automotive segment, reflecting a shift in consumer demand ahead of upcoming new model launches. The group said it remained focused on enhancing operational efficiency, strengthening cost discipline and expanding its revenue base to support long-term sustainability.

items.title: Imelda, Modi and Jollibee: Lighter side of Trump's Manila trip
items.summary: MANILA: US President Donald Trump was only in Manila for 21 hours on his whirlwind Asia trip, but that was long enough for an awkward encounter with a world leader and some local fast food. Modi asks. Modi eventually appeared resigned to his fate as he waited for Trump.

items.title: Appeals Court raises teacher's jail term to 10 years for child sex offence
items.summary: "We set aside the sentence imposed by the High Court and substitute it with eight years' imprisonment for the offence under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, and a further two years' imprisonment under Section 16(1) of the same Act, together with two strokes of the rotan. "The court also orders the respondent to undergo counselling and police supervision for two years upon completion of his prison sentence," said Justice Mohamed Zaini. The panel dismissed Ahnaf Afiq's appeal against his conviction and sentence imposed by the Muar High Court on March 11, 2026.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM NOV 18, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's 30-stock index closed in the red dragged by losses in plantation and financial services heavyweights. The key index dropped more than eight points to 1,566. In the crypto exchange, Bitcoin rose to RM266,019.

items.title: Ringgit ends lower against greenback, major currencies amid hawkish US rate outlook
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended lower against the greenback and other major and regional currencies on Wednesday, amid a hawkish US interest rate outlook. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said traders were still assessing the implications of monetary policy developments for 2026, with their immediate focus on the US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting scheduled for Dec 8-9. He said Malaysia's latest third-quarter (3Q) 2026 gross domestic product growth came in higher than the advance estimate, bringing growth for the first nine months of the year to 5.6 per cent, compared with 4.8 per cent in the corresponding period last year.

items.title: Black panther "Mek Seri" rescued after struggling to walk in Maran
items.summary: The four-year-old female, named Mek Seri, was rescued by the Peninsular Malaysia Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) and sent to the National Wildlife Rescue Centre (NWRC) in Sungkai, Perak, for further examination. Pahang Perhilitan director Yusoff Shariff said the department received information from the plantation management around noon about the animal's condition. He said six Perhilitan personnel, accompanied by a veterinary officer, were deployed to the plantation to assess the panther.

items.title: Willownex secures RM28.8mil worth of contracts in Singapore
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Willownex Bhd, formerly known as Willowglen MSC Bhd, has secured three contracts worth a combined RM28.8 million in Singapore for security and surveillance systems. The largest contract, worth RM11.97 million, was awarded by Woh Hup Engineering Pte Ltd for the supply, installation, testing, commissioning and maintenance of a security system. SP PowerAssets also awarded Willowglen Services a RM6.38 million contract for the comprehensive maintenance of an integrated security and operations surveillance system.

items.title: Ahmad Maslan apologises to Anwar over 'kencing' remark in pantun
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan has apologised to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over his choice of words in a pantun recited during a Dewan Rakyat session on Monday. In a letter dated Nov 17 and received by the Prime Minister's Office today, Ahmad acknowledged that the wording was inappropriate for a government member. Ahmad said he had no intention of undermining or disrupting ties within the unity government led by Anwar.

items.title: Inari Amertron's Q1 net profit rises 18.5pct to RM61mil on higher revenue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Inari Amertron Bhd's net profit rose 18.5 per cent to RM61 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM51.5 million a year earlier, supported by higher revenue. Revenue increased 13.1 per cent to RM368.5 million from RM325.8 million in the same period, mainly driven by higher loading volumes across all business segments. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
